correctness.rationale: Cauchy formula for (d-1)-volume of a box shadow gives weighted |normal|. The only minima lie at shortest-face coordinate poles. In each pole chart the sphere density is (1-|x|^2)^(-1/2), the event is a weighted tangent crosspolytope x=O(t), and its volume gives the exact normalized leading coefficient. The first curvature term uses a uniformly expanded radial root and second moments of Dirichlet(1,...,1) simplex proportions. Moving weights w(t)=w0+lambda t+o(t) give uniformly compact tangent supports and L1 convergence of unnormalized densities, hence total-variation convergence after normalization. Signs are independent by orthant reflections; normalized magnitudes plus slack form a standard Dirichlet vector. Direct substitution verifies the dimension-four cubic crossover. Finite numerical checks corroborate, but are not used as infinite proof.

Full inspected reports on boxes and cubes cover the opposite upper endpoint, and three-dimensional scalar laws are explicitly excluded. value.rationale: Competing near-minimal facets of a high-dimensional orthotope are a natural degeneracy in rare hyperplane-shadow sampling. The sharp t-scale separation produces a nontrivial (d-1)-power crossover in the actual rare-event probability and the conditional probability of the responsible facet; the theorem additionally identifies the full correlated tangent direction and remaining budget in a Dirichlet law, enabling direct rare-orientation sampling. The fixed-weight second term controls curvature bias not captured by the tangent cone. This is not a mere unnamed parameter slice, one simulated value, or a corollary of scalar width moments; exact weighted marked conditional geometry is its central utility.
